schema_version.description: The packet identity this packet records. "1.0" is the released packet: it never carries inputs.worker_job. "1.1" is the released job-capable packet (CD-0205): it may carry inputs.worker_job when the dispatcher selected a ready worker-job revision. "2.0" is the current card-free packet: the retired domain_cards member is refused, and it is the only identity a live dispatch may record.

report_protocol.description: Dispatch-owned final-report framing, covered by the authorized packet digest. New builders pin this protocol; absence identifies historical legacy output. This is not report schema or worker identity.

review_input.description: Dispatch-owned input candidate and exact criterion/architecture revisions judged by Review. Required by core admission for candidate-bound Review, and refused on other lanes.

context.description: Prose context a packet built before the typed record members carried. The lane-packet schema keeps it so a retained packet from an attempt dispatched before that change still validates on recovery. The core dispatch admission refuses it, so no new packet carries it.

law_context.description: The approved contract's binding law and Domains the pinned continuity resolved. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet member differs from the current recorded state, omits a present record, or carries a member no record backs.

design_record.description: The current typed design record (CD-0128). The core refuses a dispatch whose packet member differs from the current recorded state, omits a present record, or carries a member no record backs.

proposal_record.description: The recorded proposal's problem, user outcomes, and constraints. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet member differs from the current recorded state, omits a present record, or carries a member no record backs.

source_event_id.description: The durable failure, rejection, or correction-request event that opened this correction. The diagnosis and strategy are that event's directions. The core refuses a packet whose correction names a different source than the current correction.

work_context.description: The current work-context view the work pin carried when the packet was built. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet does not consume the current view byte-for-byte, exactly as it refuses a packet that skips a durable correction.

checkpoint.description: The latest context checkpoint the pinned continuity projection carried when the packet was built, with its durable identity. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet does not carry the latest checkpoint byte-for-byte; its strategy and diagnosis are coordinator directions to follow.

size.description: The recorded work size and its model/operator provenance at dispatch. Omitted when unsized; never inferred from the objective or job line estimate.

lane_work_size_summary.description: The work item's current effective size, model decision, optional operator override, model version, and recording time. Absent when work has never been sized.

review_candidate.description: Review's candidate claim. Acceptance derives authority from the admitted input and the host's clean terminal observation, not these claims.

objective_source.description: Where inputs.task came from: contract_premise is the approved contract premise carried verbatim; work_question is the recorded work question carried before contract approval.

contract_version.description: The applicable contract version, or null when no contract applies.

assigned_result.description: The one evidence obligation whose discharge completes this attempt, derived from the registered lane.

predicate_id.description: The store refuses a predicate_id without the "predicate:" prefix. Write ids in the form "predicate:<name>".

lane_packet_worker_job.description: The selected ready worker-job revision this attempt executes (CD-0205). The core refuses a packet whose worker_job is not a ready recorded revision with this exact content, and refuses the member on a pinned definition that predates worker jobs. inputs.task stays the complete parent contract premise; this object bounds the attempt's own objective.

acceptance_oracle.description: The owner-level acceptance oracle of the selected revision: the one oracle copy every admitted lane receives. Optional and omitted on every revision a pre-oracle definition recorded. The core refuses a packet whose worker_job differs from the recorded ready revision, oracle included.

direct_caller_allowance.description: The recorded conditional direct-caller scope of the selected revision (CD-0227 D1). Optional and omitted on every read-only revision.

project_id.description: The permitted Project: always the recorded job's project_scope.

mechanisms.description: The changed owner mechanisms the caller repair preserves.

domain_ids.description: The approved affected Domains of the active parent contract the allowance keeps.

law_bindings.description: The pinned law revisions the allowance keeps, possibly empty.

caller_exclusions.description: The measured paths of the work's other jobs currently in correction. The core computes this set and refuses a packet whose exclusions differ; only the implementation capability class carries it, and it never enters the job digest.

lane_worker_checks_repair.description: Core-recorded checks repair: the stated reason and each named revision's exact binding and old checks. The containing job's checks are the new checks. Present only on repair-capable recorded revisions, covered by their immutable digest.

lane_worker_oracle_mechanism.description: The source-level owner of one obligation: the Project that owns the repository, one contained source path, and the symbol or entry point that owns the behavior.

path.description: A normalized relative repository-contained source path.

recipe_source.description: The exact pinned recipe manifest, not the candidate's modified harness. Native preparation resolves its file bytes, cwd, build-selected witnesses, and environment without test execution. Dispatch consumes that qualified preparation, never an automatic compiler or control run.

argv.description: The exact argument vector of the control, never shell text.

readiness_evidence_refs.description: The qualified native preparation run references for this exact owner/case/control bundle, parent contract, Project, raw subject, and environment. A legacy green command, unrelated evidence binding, compilation assertion, or zero-selector control is not readiness.

lane_worker_acceptance_oracle.description: The owner-level acceptance oracle of one immutable worker-job revision, carried verbatim from the recorded job. Every bound mirrors internal/store AcceptanceOracle exactly.

lane_worker_oracle_receipt.description: One typed control-execution receipt, mirroring contracts/agent-lane-report.schema.json $defs/oracle_receipt exactly: reported evidence, never native-run authority. A retained receipt is a prior-subject regression baseline; subject_commit is the host-derived raw OID, filled only from the packet's core work context. A timeout is unavailable evidence, not a measured failure.

subject_commit.description: Host-derived raw commit OID. Dispatch-owned: a worker-authored value is stripped before the canonical report; only the core work-context subject supplies it.

recipe_source.description: The exact pinned harness identity a receipt executed: a repository file at an exact commit. A receipt names the recipe the control pinned, never the candidate's modified copy of the harness.

exit_code.description: Required exactly when result is pass or fail: the control's exit status.

run_ref.description: The immutable native-run or artifact locator of the execution. Nonempty exactly when result is pass or fail; a not_run or unavailable result carries the empty string and names its explanation in evidence_refs. Never invent a locator: when no producing route issued one, result is unavailable and run_ref stays empty.

lane_worker_oracle_finding.description: The typed oracle tie of one review finding, mirroring contracts/agent-lane-report.schema.json $defs/oracle_finding exactly: a closed classification plus the owner, predicate/law, case, and control references that bind it. Classification and severity are different dimensions; the tie records no acceptance.

classification.description: delivery_blocker: a failed obligation of a declared owner. uncovered_case: a legitimate new entry path the inventory omitted — a real blocker, not a rejection. follow_up: outside the approved owner/contract; never an open repair criterion. oracle_defect: the harness itself is obsolete, inconsistent, or unsound; it blocks readiness, not a fabricated repair.

evidence_refs.description: The reproducible evidence that supports the finding. A known control failure names that control's receipt.

entry_point.description: For an uncovered_case: the explicit new entry path or transition the inventory omitted.

continues_finding_id.description: The earlier ranked finding of this work that this finding continues. Same failure, same canonical open identity; an uncertain join becomes a new finding and earns no shrink credit.

variant_of.description: The owner-family finding this newly reproduced alternate entry path is a variant of. A variant is a new identity, not the same open finding.

lane_native_oracle_stream.description: Native producer descriptor only. One raw BLOB per stream stays on the existing verify lease. A complete ref requires atomic full capture; incomplete and abandoned output cannot supply full-output acceptance. Preview truncation does not imply stream truncation.

recipe_kind.description: The closed discriminator of the target-runner family. Its presence marks a target preparation; a Go preparation never carries it.

target_materializer.description: The closed materializer axis. It owns dependency manifest and lockfile equality with the pinned recipe, offline lock-verified materialization into per-run scratch, cached-byte integrity, disabled scripts, and the runtime fingerprints. none declares a dependency-free recipe.

target_runner.description: The closed runner axis. It owns collection, the exact witness population, and the result grammar; check pins each declared check's full bounded argv and grades the host-observed exit status.

selected_witness_ids.description: The runner-defined exact witness identities the qualified preparation selected: unique bounded visible strings of at most 256 bytes. The rendered selector still obeys the bounded verify command shape, so the nominal maximum derives from the shared witness allowance, not an independent one. No truncation or omitted witness.

case_to_witness_map.description: Each control case maps to 1 to 8 selected witness IDs; the map covers exactly the control's cases, and the union of its values is exactly selected_witness_ids.

selected_test_names.description: The nominal maximum derives from floor((256-13)/6), not an independent test allowance. Every rendered selector still obeys sum(name bytes)+N+13 <= 256. No truncation or omitted witness.

oneOf.description: The pure-Go family: the legacy selected test names and case map, with no target-runner host property.

The target_runner_v1 family: the closed materializer/runner pair and the real selected witness population, never fabricated Go test names. Exactly three pairs are admitted; every other combination refuses as unsupported.
uv materializes the pinned dependencies offline; pytest collects the pinned node IDs.
none declares a dependency-free recipe; check grades each declared check's host-observed exit status.
uv materializes the pinned dependencies offline; check grades each declared check's host-observed exit status.

bun materializes the pinned bun.lock closure offline from integrity-verified cached npm tarballs, with no package manager or lifecycle script; check grades each declared check's host-observed exit status.

lane_native_oracle_preparation.description: The store-selected qualified preparation for an immutable job's exact readiness reference, never a latest-run guess or worker assertion. Two closed recipe families share the record and one branch must match exactly: a mixed family shape, an unknown recipe kind, or an unsupported materializer/runner pair refuses. The pure-Go family proves exact pinned file bytes, cwd, build-selected nonempty witnesses, and compile-only readiness; non-Go and resolved embed inputs must be declared pinned fixtures or explicit compiler inputs, with no production Go/module replacement. The target_runner_v1 family admits exactly the pairs uv+pytest, none+check, uv+check, and bun+check: the materializer owns dependency manifest and lockfile equality with the pinned recipe, offline lock-verified materialization into per-run scratch, cached-byte integrity, disabled lifecycle and build scripts, and runtime fingerprints (none declares a dependency-free recipe); the runner owns collection, the exact witness population, and the result grammar, and preparation runs only its collection or check-input stage, never the graded workload. No Vitest or pnpm surface exists. Every stage pins its installed toolchain; the Go stages set GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off, GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly, CGO_ENABLED=0, GOWORK=off, and a private disposable GOCACHE. No aggregate scratch quota or uncommitted-diagnostics promise. Preparation grants no worker attempt, verification authority, or semantic acceptance.

lane_work_context_view.description: The core reader's current work-context view, carried verbatim from the work pin. Every bound mirrors internal/store WorkContextView exactly.

source_event_frontier.description: The highest sequence among the work item's context-source events (declarations and terminal worker reports) the view was assembled at.

research_findings.description: The selected research entries the latest declaration anchor resolved, in authored order, beside the generic findings under the shared 32-finding bound. Omitted when the declaration selects nothing.

oracle_receipts.description: The prior typed control-execution receipts this work retained, in log order: reported regression baselines with their exact identities, never current-subject acceptance.

oracle_preparations.description: Only native preparation records selected by the immutable job's readiness refs. No raw output or alternative readiness authority.

subject_commit.description: The sole core-derived current subject, as a raw commit OID. Native receipt subject_ref remains commit:OID and the store normalizes that reference once.

path.description: A normalized relative repository-contained path at the pinned commit; read the pinned Git bytes, not the changed checkout.

finding_id.description: Core-derived from the source event sequence and ordinal; never authored.

kind.description: The generic claim vocabulary of an authored finding. A ranked oracle finding projects the empty kind: its identity is the oracle tie, never a generic claim class.

evidence_refs.description: The evidence that supports the finding. A ranked finding without an oracle tie projects null; the core reader owns that wire shape.

status.description: A finding is a reported claim, never acceptance. The open status names a ranked review finding the lineage currently holds open: still a claim, and open.

source_kind.description: Present only on a ranked review finding: the entry carries an oracle tie and rides the open-set lineage, never the generic worker-claim notebook.

oracle.description: The typed oracle tie of a ranked review finding: classification plus the owner, predicate/law, case, and control references that bind it.

product_wide_rationale.description: Present exactly when the declared Domain is the registry's root Domain; the core validates that pairing at authoring.

lane_work_context_research_selection.description: One closed selected research reference: the exact pack, revision, and finding beside the declared Domain. References only, never research content.

scopes.description: The finding's own applicability scopes, carried unchanged from the research authority. The Go reader always serializes this member, so the context projection requires it.

lane_work_context_research_finding.description: The native research finding a resolved context entry carries: the research authority's own vocabulary, never mapped to generic worker observations or invented evidence refs.

lane_research_scopes.description: The native research scope vocabulary: applicability, never authority. Mode home applies to the owner's home broadly; explicit applies to exactly the declared lists.

lane_research_source.description: The native research source descriptor, carried exactly as the research authority publishes it.

view_id.description: Core-derived from the selection event sequence and ordinal; a separate namespace from the generic finding ids, never authored.

selection_event_id.description: The event that authored the reference, never a claim that the research body came from that event.

required.description: Derived from the consuming work's present binding; an absent binding is fail-closed required because absence cannot establish optional reliance.

sources.description: Every linked source descriptor once, sorted by source id, and no unrelated source. An unsourced finding stays an empty array.

view_id.description: Core-derived from the selection event sequence and ordinal; a separate namespace from the generic finding ids, never authored.

selection_event_id.description: The event that authored the reference, never a claim that the research body came from that event.

required.description: Derived from the consuming work's present binding; an absent binding is fail-closed required because absence cannot establish optional reliance.

state.description: The typed drift states: an unresolved entry carries references and provenance only, no finding and no sources.

lane_work_context_research_finding_view.description: One selected research entry of the shared work-context view. Exactly the resolved state carries the native finding and its linked source descriptors; every other state carries the closed selection tuple and provenance only.

items.description: The closed view-id namespace: generic finding ids and selected research view ids share the group's ordered id list. Generic finding_refs never resolve research.

domain_cards.description: Retired member, retained only so the released 1.0/1.1 shapes still validate on replay and retained-result recovery: the version branches below require it on those identities and refuse it on the current 2.0. No live reader produces cards and no live producer may record them.

lane_context_checkpoint.description: The owning continuity reader's latest context checkpoint, carried verbatim from the pinned continuity projection. Every bound mirrors internal/store ContextCheckpoint exactly; the projection carries no source event identity, so checkpoint_id, work_version, and sequence are the durable identity.

strategy.description: Coordinator direction the worker follows for this attempt.

items.description: A workflow reference list item: whitespace-free, 2-128 chars, matching the store's ValidReference. Slashes are allowed because touched refs name repository paths.
A workflow reference list item: whitespace-free, 2-128 chars, matching the store's ValidReference.

lane_law_context.description: The approved contract's binding law and Domains, resolved at continuity read time from the law_subjects and domains projections. Absent when the contract binds no law and no Domain.

registry_path.description: The repository path of the Domain registry shard. Present when the context binds at least one Domain, so a dispatched lane reads Domain structure from the file instead of a Concord tool.

roles.description: Every binding role the approved contract gives the law, sorted and deduplicated.

obligation_ids.description: The contract's verification obligations that name the law, sorted and deduplicated. Present only when roles carries obligation.

kind.description: The law_subjects record kind. Constitution records are law-bearing and project into law_subjects, so a contract can mandate them.

criteria.description: The law's acceptance criteria bound to the reading work item's own outcome predicates (CD-0180). Present only when at least one criterion binds this work item.

lane_proposal_record.description: The recorded proposal fields the dispatched lane packet renders. Absent when no proposal is recorded.

lane_work_record.description: The work item's recorded value statement, task, and narrative, each verbatim and present exactly when the recorded text is not blank. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet member differs from the recorded work item.

subject.description: Bounds: 1..1024 code points inclusive; <=1024 UTF-8 bytes inclusive
